To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the adversarial bandit problem can be reduced to a convex optimization problem and that 2) this reduction allows us to design an efficient algorithm for adversarial bandits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning from a set of bandit instances, where the learner has no control over the instances.
the design and analysis of efficient online algorithms for a variety of problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adversarial bandit is a more challenging problem than the stochastic bandit.
, the adversarial bandits are a generalization of the stochastic bandits.
there is no single best algorithm, but rather a best algorithm for each specific scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the adversarial bandit model is not only a useful abstraction of online learning problems, but also a useful tool to analyze the performance of other learning algorithms.
the optimal policy for the MAB is the policy which chooses the arm that maximizes the expected reward.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the regret for the MAB problem is proportional to the square-root of the number of arms, not the number of instances.
, in many cases, the best strategy for solving a MAB problem is to solve it in parallel with other instances of the same problem.
the performance of a single MAB instance is not a good predictor of the performance of the overall system.
